scenarios.name: Discuss then decide: memory only? No, keep Room

card.problem: Design offline caching for the feed using Room
card.heard: Design offline caching for the feed, using Room
card.say: Okay, I'll design the feed cache with Room. First I want to agree on the scope. The feed shows a list of posts, and each post has an id, text, author and timestamp. When the network is down, the user should still see the last feed they loaded. New posts load when the connection comes back.
card.type: add@FeedCache: @Entity(tableName = "feed_post") ⏎ data class FeedPostEntity( ⏎     @PrimaryKey val id: String, ⏎     val author: String, ⏎     val text: String, ⏎     val createdAt: Long ⏎ ) ⏎  ⏎ @Dao ⏎ interface FeedPostDao { ⏎     @Query("SELECT * FROM feed_post ORDER BY createdAt DESC") ⏎     fun observeFeed(): Flow<List<FeedPostEntity>> ⏎  ⏎     @Insert(onConflict = OnConflictStrategy.REPLACE) ⏎     suspend fun upsertAll(posts: List<FeedPostEntity>) ⏎ }
card.then: Next I'd add the database class and the repository that reads from the DAO and writes network results into it.

card.problem: Design offline caching for the feed using Room
card.say: Yes, we could, but memory only loses the feed when the app is killed. Room keeps it on disk, so the user still sees the last feed after a restart. If we only need a short cache for the current session, an in-memory list is simpler and faster. Which one do you want here?

card.problem: Design offline caching for the feed using Room
card.adopted: Keep Room for the feed cache
card.say: Okay, I'll keep Room as the cache. So the feed reads from Room first, and the network fills it in the background. The user sees the last feed right away, even after the app is killed.
